To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most consistent detection of EscherichicoliO157:H7 in inoculated apple juice was provided by the use of IMS-SMA after 8 h or IMS-PCR after overnight enrichment.
the Ab-DEFT assay is the fastest and the IMS-PCR assay is the most sensitive of the assays evaluated.
Ab-DEFT was superior to IMS-PCR, IMS-SMA, and SMA, and that IMS-PCR was superior to IMS-SMA and SMA for detection of 0 CFU/ml of E. coli O 157:H7 in enriched apple juice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of rapid methods for detecting low numbers of E. coli O 157:H7 in food and food processing environments.
the development of a method for rapid and sensitive detection of the pathogen in apple juice.
the development of rapid and sensitive methods for the detection of E. coli O 157:H7 in juice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most sensitive method was IMS-PCR followed by IMS-SMA, Ab-DEFT (with enrichment), and then SMA.
IMS-PCR is the most sensitive assay for detection of E. coli O15:7:H7 in apple juices.
the Ab-DEFT assay is the method of choice for rapid detection and quantitation of E. coli O15:H7 in apple juices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IMS-PCR method was most sensitive and specific and was the most rapid method for the detection of E. coli O 157:H7 in the apple juice enrichments.
IMS-SMA, Ab-DEFT or IMS-PCR are the best methods to detect low levels of E. coli O 157:H7 in inoculated apple juice, whereas SMA is not recommended for this application.

IMS-PCR and IMS-SMA were the most rapid methods for detecting the presence of E. coli O 157:H7 in inoculated apple juice, and Ab-DETT and IMS-PCR were the most reliable methods for detecting low levels of the organism in juice stored for 28 days at 4 degreesC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of enrichment and immunomagnetic separation (IMS) can be very useful for the detection of E. coli O 157:H7 at low levels in juice.
the IMS-PCR and IMS-SMA methods provide a sensitive and rapid means of detecting low numbers of E. coli O 157:H7 from apple juice enrichments.
enrichment is necessary for detection of E. coli O:157:H7 in juice, and the most efficient enrichment is achieved by centrifugation and incubation of the pellet at 37 degreesC in nonselective broth.
